entries.name: Pelvic health
entries.definition: The care of the pelvic organs and muscles, including bladder, bowel and sexual function, pregnancy-related changes and pelvic pain.

entries.name: Penology
entries.definition: The study of punishment for crime and of the management and rehabilitation of prisoners.

entries.name: PerformanceAnalytics
entries.definition: An R package of functions for analysing the performance and risk of financial portfolios, such as returns, drawdowns and risk-adjusted ratios.

entries.name: Perinatology
entries.definition: The branch of medicine that cares for mothers and babies around the time of birth, especially in high-risk pregnancies.

entries.name: Perioperative care
entries.definition: The care of a patient before, during and after surgery.

entries.name: Periscope
entries.definition: A live video-streaming app owned by Twitter, which Twitter shut down in 2021.

entries.name: Periscope Data
entries.definition: A cloud data-analytics platform that lets analysts run SQL, Python and R against company data and build dashboards.

entries.name: Permit to work
entries.definition: A formal written system that authorises specific hazardous work, such as hot work or confined-space entry, only after the hazards are checked and controls are set.

entries.name: Personal Communications Service
entries.definition: A class of digital wireless telephone services in the US, operating in the 1.9 GHz band and licensed by the Federal Communications Commission from the 1990s.

entries.name: Personal income tax
entries.definition: The tax charged on an individual's income, such as wages, interest and investment gains.

entries.name: Personal Printer Data Stream
entries.definition: IBM's command set for controlling its printers, also supported by some other makers' printers in an emulation mode.

entries.name: Personal protective equipment
entries.definition: Clothing and gear, such as gloves, masks, goggles and hard hats, worn to protect against workplace hazards.

entries.name: Personalization
entries.definition: Tailoring content, products or experiences to individual users based on their data or behaviour.

entries.name: PEST analysis
entries.definition: A framework for reviewing the political, economic, social and technological factors that affect a business.

entries.name: Pet insurance
entries.definition: Insurance that pays all or part of the veterinary costs when a pet is ill or injured.

entries.name: Pet insurance sales
entries.definition: Selling pet insurance policies to customers.

entries.name: Petrography
entries.definition: The branch of geology that describes and classifies rocks by their mineral content and texture, usually under a microscope.

entries.name: Phalcon
entries.definition: A PHP web framework delivered as a compiled C extension, for speed and low resource use.

entries.name: PhantomJS
entries.definition: A headless web browser scripted with JavaScript, used for automated testing and page rendering, which is no longer actively developed.

entries.name: Pharmaceutical batch documentation
entries.definition: Preparing, completing and reviewing the batch records that show how each batch of a medicine was made, tested and released.

entries.name: Pharmacogenetics
entries.definition: The study of how a person's inherited genetic differences affect their response to drugs.

entries.name: Pharmacoinformatics
entries.definition: The use of computing and data analysis to study drugs, how they act in the body and how they are used.

entries.name: Pharmacy operations
entries.definition: Running the day-to-day work of a pharmacy, such as dispensing, inventory, billing and staffing.

entries.name: Philosophy of religion
entries.definition: The branch of philosophy that examines religious beliefs and concepts, such as the existence of God, evil, faith and religious language.

entries.name: Philosophy of science
entries.definition: The branch of philosophy that studies the foundations, methods and implications of science, such as what counts as evidence and explanation.

entries.name: Photo retouching
entries.definition: Editing a photograph to remove flaws and improve its appearance, such as blemishes, colour and lighting.

entries.name: PHP frameworks
entries.definition: Software frameworks for building web applications in PHP, such as Laravel, Symfony and CodeIgniter.

entries.name: phpBB
entries.definition: Free, open-source forum (bulletin board) software written in PHP.

entries.name: phpDesigner
entries.definition: A code editor and integrated development environment for PHP, from MPSoftware, for Windows.

entries.name: phpdocx
entries.definition: A PHP library for creating and editing Word (.docx) documents from code.

entries.name: PhpED
entries.definition: A commercial integrated development environment for PHP from NuSphere.

entries.name: PHPExcel
entries.definition: A PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files such as Excel; it is no longer maintained and was replaced by PhpSpreadsheet.

entries.name: phpFox
entries.definition: Commercial PHP software for building social-networking websites.

entries.name: phpGroupWare
entries.definition: Open-source groupware software, written in PHP, with a calendar, contacts, email and other shared tools.

entries.name: phpLDAPadmin
entries.definition: A web-based tool, written in PHP, for browsing and administering LDAP directories.

entries.name: phpList
entries.definition: Open-source newsletter and mailing-list manager written in PHP.

entries.name: PHPMailer
entries.definition: A PHP library for sending email, including through SMTP, with HTML bodies and attachments.

entries.name: phpPgAdmin
entries.definition: A web-based tool, written in PHP, for administering PostgreSQL databases.

entries.name: PHPUnit
entries.definition: A unit-testing framework for PHP, in the xUnit family.

entries.name: phpWebSite
entries.definition: An open-source content management system written in PHP.
